title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes 'atlas' as a set with an order <= and a stronger relation << (read: 'is well inside'), subject to axioms At 1, At 2, At 3, ... Sub-objects are 'parties fermées', 'sous-atlas' and 'sous-atlas spacieux'. Elements are 'figures'; later come 'ombres' and 'multiombres'.

The page finishes a remark begun on p. 43: sub-structure notions are transitive and hereditary along a chain of inclusions F'' ⊂ F' ⊂ F of nonempty closed parts.
(i) Spaciousness. Under the standing assumption that F' is spacious in F, F'' is spacious in F' iff it is spacious in F. This mirrors the p. 43 statement 'pourvu que l'on suppose F' spacieux'.
(ii) Sub-atlases. If F is an atlas and F' a sub-atlas, the sub-atlases of F' are exactly the sub-atlases of F contained in F'. The reason is that the extra condition beyond closedness (the 'condition 2' of the definition) is intrinsic to F''. It is just axiom At 3 for F'' with the induced relations, so it does not matter whether it is formulated relative to F' or to F.
Hence:
- (1.50) Sousat(F') = {F'' ∈ Sousat(F) | F'' ⊂ F'}.
- (1.51) For F' spacious in F: Sousatspac(F') = {F'' ∈ Sousatspac(F) | F'' ⊂ F'}.
In modern terms, the posets of sub-objects of a sub-object are the down-sets (slices) of the sub-object poset. This is the usual 'subspace of a subspace' compatibility.

Second remark: a trivial example of an atlas, announced on p. 45 as 'exemple trivial d'atlas'.
- An ordered set satisfying At 1–At 2 is equivalently described as a triple (M, <=, F). Here (M, <=) is a poset and F is a family of closed parts of M ('ens. des parties fermées') such that:
  1) F covers M: every x ∈ M lies in some F ∈ F;
  2) F is closed under passing to closed subparts: if F ∈ F and G is a closed part of F, then G ∈ F.
- Put << := <= on M. If (M, <=) satisfies At 3, then (M, <=, <<) satisfies At 1–At 7.
So the 'degenerate' choice, where well-inside coincides with the order, gives atlases. This is a sanity-check model before the non-trivial examples.

The next page returns to plane shadows and multishadows and introduces axiom At γ. That axiom says the open shadow omb(X) minus omb(∂X) is nonempty, a 'cells have nonempty interior' condition.
errors: The first sentence as transcribed ('si F'' est spacieux dans F', il l'est dans F, et la réciproque est vraie si F' est spacieux dans F') is probably meant with F' spacious in F as a standing hypothesis for both directions. Without it, spaciousness in F' need not imply spaciousness in F. This is a minor imprecision of formulation, not a real error.
The transcription has 'contenus dans F''' where the sense requires 'contenus dans F''.

ideas.what: Transitivity/heredity of sub-atlas and spacious sub-atlas notions along chains of inclusions; formulas (1.50), (1.51)
ideas.modern_name: Sub-objects of a sub-object = sub-objects contained in it (slice of a subobject poset)

ideas.what: Description of an atlas satisfying the first axioms as a poset M with a covering family of closed parts stable under closed subparts; trivial atlas with << = <=
ideas.modern_name: Covering down-closed family of 'figures' in a poset; degenerate interior relation (cf. way-below / well-inside relations in point-free topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; related relations: Scott (way-below, 1972), proximity / contact algebras (Efremovič, de Vries)

missed.claim: The whole 'Analysis situs' axiomatics, of which this page is a routine fragment, works with an order <= plus a 'well-inside' relation << on figures, with boundaries and nonempty interiors. This is structurally close to region-based / point-free topology: de Vries contact algebras, mereotopology, and the way-below relation of continuous lattices. That link does not seem to be made in the literature on Grothendieck's tame-topology program. This page itself only contains bookkeeping toward it.
missed.quote: Prenons dans M la relation ≪ =dfn ≤. Alors, si (M,≤) satisfait At 3, alors (M,≤,≪) satisfait At 1 : At 7.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could situate Grothendieck's unpublished 'tame topology' axiomatics relative to existing point-free and mereotopological frameworks. This is a weak, programmatic connection rather than a result on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine bookkeeping: heredity of sub-atlas notions, and a trivial example where << equals <=. Its only interest is as part of the largely unknown 1986 axiomatic Analysis situs.
transcription_corrections: 'la condition supplémentaire [...] 2' -> refers to condition 2 of the definition of sous-atlas (the struck passage on p. 43, 'Lorsque la condition [?] 2 est')
'Soit (F,≤) [?] un ensemble [?] satisfaisant' -> 'Soit (F,≤) un ordonné satisfaisant'
'𝔓𝔣(M)' is glossed in the margin as 'ens. des parties fermées de M'
Final 'Pour mi[...]' continues on p. 45, probably 'Pour mémoire, parmi les exemples qui vont suivre...'
